description: mylang/__main__.py reads a source file from the command line, runs it through the evaluator, prints the result, and reports file and language errors cleanly.

steps.description: This is `mylang/__main__.py`, the command-line interface (CLI) entry point. The page says the special `__main__.py` module makes `python3 -m mylang` work as an alternative to the `mylang` command. It imports `sys` and the relative import `.evaluator` for `run` and `LangError`; the page says the relative import works because `mylang` is a proper package.
`main` first checks the argument count. `len(sys.argv) != 2` means the user did not pass exactly one file. It prints a usage line to stderr and exits with status 1.
The `try` block opens the file named on the command line, reads the source, passes it to `run`, and prints the result when it is not `None`.

The `except` blocks handle failures. `FileNotFoundError` prints that the file was not found and exits. `LangError` prints the error message and exits. The page says `LangError` should be the base exception class your evaluator raises for runtime and parse errors.
The `__main__` guard calls `main()` when the file runs as a program.

title: The Command-Line Entry Point
